The '''Cratis Network''' (''Cratis Imperis''), commonly known as the Cratis, is a global network of networks using the same data relay protocol for communication.

The origins of the Cratis date back to the early 20th century but it wasn't until the 1950s and 1960s where engineers operating on prototype versions of the network were able to develop the protocols that form the foundation of the modern Cratis. In 1965, the University administration instituted universal protocols for all networks of academic computer networks. Access to this single network of networks was offered to students attending all connected universities and academies.

The '''criminal justice system of Caphiria''' is part of the [[Judiciary of Caphiria]]. Responsibility for criminal law and criminal justice in Caphiria is handled by the [[Ministry of Justice (Caphiria)|Ministry of Justice]]. Caphiria's criminal justice system features three primary tiers - the investigative system, the criminal court system, and the correctional system.

articles.snippet:
Canespa has a rich and deep history and a rich and deep culture comes along with that. Canespa has one of the most unique cultures in the world thanks to its isolation and will to not convert to an Occidentalized way of life. The Canespian culture is defined by its recently corporate nature while also being deeply religious. It is often seen as weird and foreign in many areas do to the completely different culture that developed in the region. It has not only been influenced by the geography of the region but has also been influenced by the past events that occurred in the region. The Canespan people are highly resilient and their culture will likely persist for centuries. If we can understand the culture of Canespa then we can come to better understand how Canespa interacts and carries itself on the world stage. Everything Canespa does can be tied back to its culture and its way of life.

articles.snippet:
[[Canespa|Canespa's]] government is one of the most unique in the world. Dominated by an industry of agriculture the state became controlled and eventually merged with the company that controlled the industry. This creates a form of government some call a Congressional Company, or Potato Republic. Either way this form of government exists no where else on the planet and is completely unique to [[Canespa]]. A government that while not a complete dictatorship, is not the most democratic either. There is even a monarch like system within the government caused by the influence of [[Canespa|Canespa's]] past.

== History ==

=== Early Canespa ===
Early [[Canespa]] was a much different time for the country. Native governments had not yet consolidated and [[Canespa]] was led by a family structure with one a man and many wives. It is theorized that there was one male in each group who was respected as the leader. [[Canespa]] needed more time to develop. By the year 100 these clans began to cons

articles.title: History_of_Canespa_and_Wasiqana
articles.snippet:
The [[History of Canespa and Wasiqana]] is long and complex and follows multiple eras with the first organized and recorded information appearing around 100 CE. With this scattered records do appear as soon as 400 BCE and are used to piece together much of early [[Culture of Canespa|Canespan]] history. [[Culture of Canespa|Canespan]] history is vary influential in the modern day as it reflects on the values of the [[Culture of Canespa|Canespan]] people and why the state acts as it does in a modern setting. As such [[Culture of Canespa|Canespan]] history is divided into distinct periods, all of which serve a purpose in defining the modern state as it exists today. 

Canespan history divided into six periods from a mainly cultural and political standpoint:

articles.title: House_Kanchi
articles.snippet:
'''House Kanchi''' is one of the five main houses of Canespa, it is the second largest House in population and in total number of senators. It is located in the far Northeast of Canespa and controls the [[Suyukuna's]] of Chincha Cuenca and Qulla Cuenca. It additionally controls the surrounding [[mikuna's]]. It is culturally the most distinct house and has had several independence movements in the past but none since the 19th century. 

== History ==

=== Formation ===
House Kanchi started out as a simple family in the central part of the Cusinaut around the bay. This family soon grew into a tribe, and eventually it became the first area in Canespa to organize and centralize into what could be considered a proto-state around the year 100. Archeological sites from this time indicate a booming civilization that followed an oral tradition similar to that of M'acunism. Several pyramids have been unearthed and early canals around the main bends of the river surrounding the House. The House q

== History and Backround ==

=== Origin ===
Canespan originates from central Varshan and is part of the Pan-Varshani language group present within North Crona and the Cusinaut. linguistic anthropologist's in Canespa theorize that the original split off came sometime during the early 4th century BC in the Papa river basin. After this the language almost isolated itself entirely and is even credited with being on of the only Cusinauti countries to independently develop a system of writing separate from other nations. The influence of this origin can not be understated in Canespan history. Varshani trade ships often visited Canespan shores due to the common language heritage the two countries shared.

articles.title: Mera_Bay
articles.snippet:
'''Mera Bay''', also known as the '''Quexten Bay''' (Canespan) is a body of water located between [[Caracua]] to the north and west and [[Canespa]] to the south and east. The Ashuk and adjacent Kilmer River drainage basins in [[Caracua]] contribute the majority of groundwater flow into the bay. It is known for its fishing industry, which supports much of [[Caracua]] as well as [[Canespa|Canespa's]] northern cities. The largest city on the bay is [[Extranjero]], [[Canespa|Canespa's]] third largest and the only city on the bay with a population of over a million permanent residents; the second is [[Kimiornee]], capital of [[Caracua]]. During winter and spring, the majority of the bay is iced over; however, the mouth of the pay remains warm enough due to the adjacent currents of the [[Ocean of Cathay]] for navigation with the assistance of icebreakers in colder years.

The Wasi King is likely one of the most distinct and recognizable features of the Canespan culture. A figure so dominant in the history of Canespan politics in that he has changed the religious identity of Canespa as a whole. Stepping into the spotlight within the 12th century the Wasi King immediately left a mark on the nation. Being the first figure to unite multiple Canespan tribes into one unity. Even later on his influence could be felt in the Canasta regime of the country. The idea of Canespa or Wasiqana as its called was created by the mere ambition of a single figure, the first personification of a figure known only as the Wasi King. The Wasi King is Canespa, and Canespa is the Wasi King. One can not survive without the other.

articles.title: Exuria
articles.snippet:
'''Exuria''' is a family of spiced wines in [[Caphirian cuisine]]. Exuria roughly translates to "the travelers wine", referring to the origin and popularity of the drink which dates back to Ancient Caphiria where it was commonly used as an "on-the-road" beverage for long travels. While the original recipe was lost to antiquity, a new version was created during the Principate based from a collection of contemporary sources. Exuria generally consists of honey, pepper, mastic, laurel, saffron, date seeds, and dates soaked in a wine. Exuria is typically prepared in large batches and is often one of the more readily available beverages throughout the Imperium.

articles.title: Geography_of_Caphiria
articles.snippet:
{{wip}}
The '''geography of Caphiria''' is classified into two broad categories: ''Caphirium Maiorem'' (Greater Caphiria) and ''Caphirium Coloniam'' (Possessions of Caphiria), with the former referring to the mainland and the latter to all of the territories and possessions of the Imperium. In the geographical sense however, it refers to just the mainland. 

Caphiria is located on [[Sarpedon]] and occupies over 6 million km² of land from the north-central coastline to the Sarpic heartland. At its territorial height, this extended to most of the entirety of the northern half of the continent. Caphiria shares its western border with two countries: [[Cartadania]] to its northwest and [[Pelaxia]] on its southwest. To the east Caphiria shares its northeast border with [[Aciria]], its east-central border with Bussdaberria, and its southeastern border with Valcenia.  

The total area of mainland Caphiria is 6,047,907 km² and has a total coastline of xxx,xxx km².

articles.title: Health_in_Caphiria
articles.snippet:
{{wip}}
'''Health in Caphiria''' refers to to the overall health of the population of the [[Imperium of Caphiria]]. In Caphiria, health is defined as "a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease and infirmity." Caphiria is known for its universal health care system, low infant mortality, relatively healthy cuisine and diet. As with any developed country, Caphiria has adequate and sufficient water and food distribution, and levels of nutrition and sanitation are high 

Generally speaking, Caphirians are part of a healthy society. The average national life expectancy in Caphiria is 81.3 years. By gender, the average is higher for women at 83.6 compared to 78.9 for men. This can be explored further by going into detail based off of social class: Obviously the Patrician class has the highest life expectancy at 86 years, the Equestrians at 81, Upper-Plebs at 78, Lower-Plebs at 76, and the Indigeni at 68 years on average.

articles.snippet:
{{wip}}
The '''history of Caphiria''' has been among the most influential to the modern world, from the spread of the Latin language and Romance languages as a result of the creation of the Imperial Church to its vast contributions to modern governments, law, politics, engineering, art, literature, architecture, technology, warfare, religion, language, and society.

Caphirian history is divided into six distinct political ages, each having its own sociological eras:
* '''''Ancient history''''' ({{circa}} 9th century BC - 369 BC) - This period covers the settlement of [[Latinic people]], which originated in [[Urlazio]] and would form the [[Adonerii civilization]]. The [[Latin Heroic Age]] saw the colonization of Latium, a geographic region along the northern coastline of Sarpedon. The city of Venceia was founded during this period as a trading hub and many foundational myths of Latinic societies emerged. articles.title: Narico
articles.snippet:
{{wip}}
'''Narico''' is a [[Province of Caphiria]] located on [[Urlazio|Caphirian Urlazio]], consisting of approximately a third of the island [[Urlazio]] located north of [[Sarpedon]]. Narico shares borders with the provinces of [[Canterra]] to its west, [[Ovetta]] and [[Netharra]] to its north, and the Urlazian Sea to its south. The [[Lariana|Kingdom of Lariana]] is to the east. With a population of aproximately 16 million, it is the 8th-smallest province in the Imperium. The capital of Narico is [[Castra Osaniovo]], which is situated on [[Sybaesa Port]], one of the primary ports for the [[Imperial Naval Fleet]]. Due to its mild climate, scenery, and gambling facilities, Narico has a status as a tourist destination and recreation centre for the wealthy and elite. Narico is known for its coastal resorts such as the [[Viridian Hotel]] in Magador, the [[Meridionali Resonare]] (Southern Echo Resort & Spa) in Castra Osaniovo, and the exclusive [[Nova Resort]] in Aldorrolan.{{Infobox settl

articles.title: National_budget_of_Caphiria
articles.snippet:
[[category:Caphiria]]
[[category:Government of Caphiria]]
[[category:Finance in Caphiria]]
The '''national budget of Caphiria''' refers to the annual revenue (money received) and expenditures (money spent) of the [[Imperium of Caphiria]]. The [[Senate (Caphiria)|Senate]] has the sole authority over the country's financial and budgetary policy, and is responsible for setting annual revenues and spending levels after approval from the [[National Assembly (Caphiria)|National Assembly]]. Once approved by the National Assembly, the government may make adjustments of up to 2% to the budget without having to seek further parliamentary approval. 

The national budget concerns only spending and revenue by the central government, which includes provincial administration but excludes regional and local budgets

articles.title: Possessions_(Caphiria)
articles.snippet:
{{politics of Caphiria |divisions}}
In [[Caphiria]], '''Possessions''' are the major overseas territories under the control of the [[Government of Caphiria|Imperium]]. Caphiria does not classify its Possessions as subdivisions of the Imperium itself; rather, each is treated in law as a separate jurisdiction. Most have their own legislatures and a degree of autonomy usually exceeding that of the autonomous provinces, including fiscal independence. Still, The Imperium retains varying degrees of responsibility in all of the territories, currently ranging from full political control to a largely ceremonial presence. The main reserved matters are the areas of diplomacy, international treaties, defense and security. Possessions of the Imperium still follow the same organization of administrative divisions, though the naming scheme may differ based on cultural and historical contexts.

There are 3 types of possessions - overseas provinces, standard possessions, protectorates.

'''Religion in ancient Caphiria''' refers to both the religious beliefs and practices of the pre-Christianized [[Caphiria]]n civilization, including the polytheistic pre-Three Sisters era dating far back to Caphiric prehistory, and the Three Sisters era between 300 BC and the 6th century AD, after which the local populations started abandoning domestic faiths in place of [[Catholic Church|Catholic]]ism, which is still practiced by Caphirians today. Caphiric religious development was heavily influenced by both the region and the native inhabitants of the Caphiria region. The seafaring nature of the [[Adonerii]] meant that their beliefs were influenced by foreign religions as a result of trade and cultural exchange with various foreign peoples.

'''Savidi Feranzi Amborchetto''' (August 29, 1899 - March 3, 1993) was a retired [[Caphirian]] astronaut, mechanical engineer, rocket scientist, and retired fighter pilot of the [[Imperial Aerial Defense Force|Caphirian Air Force]]. He was a veteran of six space flights and ranks 3rd for the amount of time a Caphirian has been in space: a total of 903 days, 19 hours, and 39 minutes. Amborchetto is best known for being in space during the [[Second Great War]] and witnessing pivotal moments such as the nuclear bombing of Paulastra.

Amborchetto died as a result of radiation poisoning in 1993 and had been in declining health for the majority of his life.

'''Air Cartadania Flight 6664''' was an Air Cartadania flight that was hijacked on 18 December 1988 by the Free Pelaxia Group of Port de Vent in the air over the Sea of Canete. The terrorists murdered five passengers and their intention was to crash the plane into the Vilauristre skyline. When the aircraft reached Collinebourg, DELTA, a counter-terror unit of the Yonderian Defence Force, stormed the plane and killed all four hijackers.

articles.title: Asylum_in_Cartadania
articles.snippet:
{{wip}}
Seeking '''asylum in Cartadania''' is a legal right for victims of political persecution stipulated in the [[Constitution of Cartadania]]. In a wider sense, the right of asylum recognizes the definition of 'refugee' as established in the 1904 Refugee Convention and is understood to protect asylum seekers from {{wp|deportation}} and grant them certain protections under the law. Generally, these protections are a part of the asylum procedure itself and are verified by the [[Office of Asylum and Migration Services]] (OAM) without any further application. The initially unlimited right of asylum was revised in essential points and also limited by a transformation of the fundamental right of asylum into an objective guarantee was demanded in order to give the state the legal opportunity to impose an upper limit or quota.

articles.title: Automotive_industry_in_Cartadania
articles.snippet:
{{wip}}
The '''automotive industry in Cartadania''' is a quite large employer in the country and is one of the most prominent in the world. Cartadania's automotive industry is best known for its automobile designs in higher-end vehicles. The industry rapidly increased from the late 1970s to the 1990s (when it was oriented both for domestic use and worldwide export) and in the 1980s and 1990s, became a production leader with up to 13 million cars per year manufactured and significant exports. It is today among the most advanced automobile-producing countries in the world.

articles.snippet:
{{Culture of Cartadania}}
'''Cartadanian culture''' is an intricate tapestry woven from the historical legacies of diverse civilizations, reflecting a fusion of early influences from northern [[Urlazio|insular Sarpedon]] and the [[Caphiria|Latinic Empire]], as well as indigenous roots. The intricate interplay of these historical threads has shaped the rich cultural landscape that defines modern [[Cartadania]]. Central to Cartadanian cultural heritage is the intersection of ancient [[Adonerum|Adonerii civilizations]], from which the Latinic Empire emerged, and the vibrant tapestry of Taínean cultures from the West. This cultural confluence has bequeathed Cartadania with a multi-layered historical foundation, infusing its artistic expressions, traditions, and societal values. The post-Latinic empire era witnessed Cartadania's endeavor to construct a pluralistic political framework, bridging conservative and liberal ideologies, albeit amid challenges. The Rianee Cooperative Reserve is a semiautonomous region composed three provinces of [[Caracua]]. Founded in 2024 after the [[Final War of the Deluge]], it acts as a preserve for the seminomadic [[List of peoples of Cusinaut#Q-T|Rianee]] people, with Rianee tribes having preferential hunting and fishing rights as well as the right to apply tribal law and land rights protections. Its landmass is largely wooded hills and tundra. It is one of the poorest and most sparsely populated regions in both countries, particularly in Maloka.

The '''Sluagh''' ({{wp|Old Irish|Gallawan}} ''slúag'', {{wp|Scottish Gaelic|Carnish Gaelic}} ''Slúagh''; {{wp|English language|Ænglish}}: 'host, army, crowd'), or '''Sluagh na marbh''' ('host of the dead'), were the hosts of the unforgiven dead in [[Carnish folklore|Carnish folklore]]. In the words of Carnish folklorist {{wp|Lewis Spence}}, "In Carna the Sluagh, or fairy host, was regarded as composed of the souls of the dead flying through the air, and the feast of the dead at Hallowe'en was likewise the festival of the fairies." Usually taking a crescent form, similar to a flight of grey birds, they were said to be able to approach and pick up a person from any direction and then transport them far away through the air, from one area of Carna to another. Although they could sometimes rescue humans lost in the wilderness, they were generally portrayed as danger

articles.title: Smoking_in_Caphiria
articles.snippet:
{{wip}}
'''Smoking in Caphiria''' is legally permitted, with certain restrictions. Smoking is restricted in most enclosed places, including indoor workplaces and indoor public places. Smoking is permitted in designated rooms in hotels, long term care homes, palliative hospices, prisons, and offshore installations such as oil rigs; and smoking is permitted for smoking cigars or pipe tobacco in specialist tobacco shops. It is also illegal to smoke in a car if one is transporting people under 18 or if a vehicle is being used for work purposes. Smoking is prevalent among a sizeable, but continuously reducing minority of the population.

Caphirian law prohibits the sale of tobacco products via vending machines, single cigarettes, small packets of cigarettes, and tobacco for oral use. The sale of tobacco products is prohibited to persons under the age of 18.

articles.title: Southern_Route
Suniberia
articles.snippet:
{{wip}}
'''Suniberia''', sometimes called the '''Cult of Suniberia''', was an ancient Caphiric ecstatic cult that originated around the 1st century AD. The cult was strongly associated with satyrs, centaurs, and sileni, and its characteristic symbols were the bull, the serpent, tigers, and wine. The cult is most notable for its usage of intoxicants and other trance-inducing techniques (like dance and music) to remove inhibitions and social constraints, liberating the individual to return to a "natural state". It also provided some liberation for men and women marginalized by Caphirian society, among which were slaves, outlaws, and non-citizens. During the third century, the practitioners of Suniberia were driven into secrecy and persecuted as heretics as the rise of Christianity pushed the various local religious traditions out. As a result, many aspects of the Suniberia cult remain unknown and were lost; modern knowledge is derived from descriptions, imagery and cross-cultural studies

articles.title: Taxation_in_Caphiria
articles.snippet:
'''Taxation in Caphiria''' is levied by the [[Government of Caphiria]] and is collected by the [[Ministry of the Treasury (Caphiria)|Ministry of the Treasury]]. In 2025, total tax revenue was 30.3% of Caphiria's GDP, or $16.1 trillion. 

While the [[Ministry_of_the_Treasury_(Caphiria)#Department_of_Taxation_and_Fiscal_Affairs|Department of Taxation and Fiscal Affairs]] (DTFA) is responsible for developing economic and public finance policies, the ''lex tributum'' (tax code), taxes, tariffs, and duties are solely set by the [[National Assembly (Caphiria)|National Assembly]]. At the same time, the [[Central Tax Service]] (within the DTFA) is responsible for tax collection. There are three types of Quaestores - ''supremus'', ''provincialis'', and ''oppidanus,'' representing national, provincial, and local tax jurisdictions.

articles.title: Ten_Year_Plan_(Caphiria)
articles.snippet:

The '''Ten Year Plan''' was a policy memorandum and later partly adopted strategy of [[Caphiria]] in the interwar period during the reign of the [[Imperator]] [[Magasevetus]]. The Plan, formulated in [[1928]], envisioned [[Lariana]] returned to Caphirian control within ten years, giving it its name. The Plan called for the escalation of tensions in [[Dericania]] in order to create a general Levantine war no later than [[1935]]; with [[Urcea]] sufficiently committed in Levantia, [[Caphiria]] would launch an invasion of Lariana and present its conquest as a ''fait accompli''. The concept of clandestine support in Dericania had been proven in [[1925]] with various socialist insurgents receiving piecemeal support from some sectors of the [[Government of Caphiria]]. '''Tepiù pugna,''' also known as '''Caphirian Cane Fighting''', is a [[Caphirian]] martial art that uses a ''tepiù'' or cane (a kind of walking-stick) designed for fighting.  The ''tepiù'' is very light, made of chestnut wood and slightly tapered. A padded suit and a fencing mask are worn for protection. ''Tepiù pugna'' was standardized in the 1957 for sporting competition by Đureș Aleorizio Cambri, a Caphirian senator.

''Tepiù pugna'' is a product of Caphirian history and culture. '''The Game''' ([[Aciria|Acirian]]: '''Il Gioco''') is a term denoting the intricate and skillful political maneuvers employed by the nobles and aristocracy of [[Aciria]]. Its origins can be traced back to the early era of the Grand Empire during the late 18th century, during which both the nobility and aristocracy engaged in smear campaigns and strategic tactics to gain favor with the newly crowned [[Emperor of Aciria|Emperor]] [[Giovanni Montefeltro|Giovanni I]]. As time progressed, these techniques evolved into a sophisticated 'game' of intrigue, serving not only to secure the Emperor's patronage but also to pursue personal political and financial aspirations. The opulent balls, hosted by the Emperor, aristocrats, or nobility, often serve as the backdrop for the unfolding of the Game. articles.title: Trinity_Defense_System
articles.snippet:
[[File:Trinity.svg|thumb|The logo for the Trinity Program]]
The '''Trinity Defense System''' (also known as '''TRINITY''' or the '''TRINITY Program''') is the national integrated aerial defence system and military program for the [[Imperium of Caphiria]]. The Trinity Defense System is a multi-layered network of overlapping systems working together alongside the three primary defense systems: MALEPHIST, The Twelve Disciples, and WORMWOOD.

MALEPHIST is a short-range laser air defense system designed to destroy short-range rockets, artillery, and mortars up to 10 km; The Twelve Disciples is a mobile all-weather air defense and C-RAM system designed to intercept and destroy short-range rockets and artillery shells fired from distances of 10 km to 300 km; WORMWOOD is the medium/long-range anti-ballistic and surface-to-air missile system designed to intercept enemy planes, drones, tactical ballistic missiles, medium- to long-range rockets and cruise missiles from 50 km to 500 km.

'''Valcenia''' was a large [[Great Levantia|Great Levantine]] {{wp|castra|fort}} in [[Kinlaig]], [[Carna]], now ruined, and which has been partially reconstructed. It was first excavated in the 1870s and all modern buildings on the site were cleared in the 1970s.  It is managed by the [[Carnish Heritage Committee]] as '''Valcenia Great Levantine Fort and Museum'''.

articles.title: Education_Standards_Assessment
articles.snippet:
The '''Verona Education Standards Assessment''' or '''VESA''' (Cartadanian: ''Avaliação dos Padrões de Educação de Verona'' or APEV) is a public school standardized testing program in the Commonwealth of Verona. It sets forth learning and achievement expectations for core subjects for grades K-12 in Verona's Public Schools. The standards represent what many teachers, school administrators, parents, and business and community leaders believe schools should teach and students should learn. The Verona Department of Education, schools, and school systems routinely receive essential feedback on the effectiveness of implementation and address effective instructional strategies and best practices.

The VES is supportive of and direct response to the Student Succession Act, which was signed into law by then-President Murilo E. Sato on January 8, 2000. They address student achievement in four critical areas: (1) Cartadanian, (2) mathematics, (3) science, and (4) history/social science. Students

articles.title: Energy_in_Cartadania
articles.snippet:
'''Energy in Cartadania''' refers to {{wp|energy development|energy}} and {{wp|electricity generation|electricity production}}, consumption, import and export in the country. The nation's energy composition draws from a quintet of key pillars: {{wp|nuclear power}}, {{wp|natural gas}}, {{wp|fossil fuel power station|liquid fuels}}, {{wp|coal}}, and {{wp|renewable energy|renewables}}. In 2030, natural gas made up the largest portion of electricity generation in the country, at around 40%, while nuclear power accounted for 27% and renewables accounted for 30% of energy consumption, the largest sector of which being {{wp|hydroelectric power}}. 

Cartadania has a unified {{wp|electrical grid|power grid}} that is strategically segmented into three distinct {{wp|wide area synchronous grid|interconnections}}, each tailored to efficiently serve specific geographic regions and utilize the diverse array of energy resources. articles.title: Governing_Apparatus_for_Integrated_Affairs
articles.snippet:
The '''Governing Apparatus for Integrated Affairs''', or '''GAIA''', is the [[Cartadania]]n [[Department of Defense (Cartadania)|Department of Defense]]'s (DoD) interconnected system of management and analytics. It essentially serves as the backbone for Cartadania's modular infrastructure network, monitoring the country's warfare systems, allowing for interconnected data and other key functions to be shared between them.

Development of GAIA began with a need to move from traditional mainframe systems due to the limitations of power on silicon. The large amounts of power drawn from the system were creating multiple issues for the facilities, thus the DoD and [[Department of Energy and Mineral Resources|DEMR]], in collaboration with [[Erudite University of Alahuela|Erudite]]'s electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, computer science, and nanophotonics teams, began {{wp|R&D}} on a new system to eliminate these bottlenecks.

It was established as a free service in 2010 to replace the previous system and is not mandatory, allowing Cartadanians to file taxes through private companies if they wish. IRIS is based on modern technologies, including {{wp|encryption}} and {{wp|digital signature}}s, to ensure the security and privacy of taxpayers' information. articles.title: PEP_Code
articles.snippet:
A '''PEP Code''' is a {{wp|postal code}} used in [[Cartadania]]. In 1905, the [[Cartadanian National Postal Service]] ({{lang-cd|Serviço Postal Nacional Cartadaniana}}; abbreviated ''SPNC'' but also known as ''Correios'') introduced a revolutionary system called the Postal Address Plan or "Plano de endereço postal" (for which PEP is short) in Cartadania. This system revolutionized the postal service by introducing a standardized format for postal addresses that used PEP Codes to identify specific locations. The PEP Code system was designed to facilitate the delivery of mail and packages by creating a more efficient and streamlined postal service.

The PEP Code system is a five-digit postal code system that assigns a unique code to each delivery area in Cartadania. articles.title: Road_signs_in_Cartadania
articles.snippet:
{{wip}}
'''Road signs in Cartadania''' represent a vital component of the nation's transportation infrastructure and safety protocols. These signs, standardized and predominantly regulated by the federal government through the [[Department of Transportation (Cartadania)|Department of Transportation]] under the banner of the ''Uniform Traffic Code'', serve as indispensable guides for motorists, pedestrians, and cyclists navigating the extensive network of roadways that crisscross the country. While the federal government lays down overarching guidelines for signage, there exists a nuanced interplay with state and territorial authorities. These subnational entities, steeped in distinct histories and legislative traditions, occasionally uphold signage codes predating or supplementing the federal directives. However, the overarching theme is one of homogeneity.

=== Federal ''estrada'' and ''interestadual'' ===
The federal highway system is split into two types of highway–''estrada'' and ''interestadual'', both managed by the [[Department of Transportation (Cartadania)|Cartadania Department of Transportation]] (CDOT). The distinction between the two kinds of federal high capacity roads is mainly a historical one, though with some very explicit reasoning for their distinction. Outside of urban areas, those differences seldom have practical consequences, though both types may still exist in rural areas. Both kinds are {{wp|divided highway}}s with {{wp|limited-access road|full access control}} and at least two lanes per direction of travel. articles.title: Telecommunications_in_Cartadania
articles.snippet:
{{Culture of Cartadania}}
'''Telecommunications in Cartadania''' are highly developed. It is served by an extensive system of automatic {{wp|telephone exchange}}s connected by modern networks of {{wp|fiber-optic}} cable, {{wp|coaxial cable}}, {{wp|microwave radio relay}}, and a domestic satellite system. The cellular telephone service is widely available, expanding rapidly to extremely rural areas, and includes roaming service to foreign countries, while those visiting countries where the operating carrier is also present continue service as usual. As a result of intensive capital expenditures, even some rural and remote areas have been rapidly modernized to the most advanced technology.

articles.title: Anthems_of_Castadilla
articles.snippet:
According to the [[Constitution of Castadilla]], there are three songs which are recognised as the '''anthems of [[Castadilla]]''' with each given anthem serving a different purpose. Since the formation of the [[Delepasian Confederation]] in 1852, Delepasia and its subsequent successor governments have had an imperial anthem, representing the [[Castadillaan Emperor|Emperor]], a commanderial anthem, representing the [[Commander-in-Chief of the Imperial Armed Forces (Castadilla)|Commander-in-Chief]] (a position currently held by the Emperor since 1994), and a national anthem, representing the nation. As of 2038, the three anthems of Castadilla are currently "{{wp|Het Wilhelmus|Mine Shield for Thee}}" as the imperial anthem, the "{{wp|El gran Carlemany|Castadillaan March}}" as the commanderial anthem, and the "{{wp|Anthem of the Estonian Soviet Socialist Republic|State Anthem of Castadilla}}" as the national anthem.

articles.snippet:
[[File:Castadillaan Anthropomorphism.png|thumb|330px|Clockwise from top-right: [[Xoel Salgado]], [[Odiseo Tarquinio]], [[Padre Maro (character)|Padre Maro]], [[Xabier Cabaleiro (character)|Xabier Cabaleiro]]]]
In [[Castadilla]], animal {{wp|anthropomorphism}} is considered to be a significant and pervasive part of the nation's [[Culture of Castadilla|culture]]. Although anthropomorphism as a concept is common throughout the [[Occident]] and the rest of the world, it has since the end of the [[Second Great War]] became increasingly associated with Castadillaan culture, particularly the [[Delepasians|Delepasian]] culture, starting with the international release of the ''[[tiras gráficas|tiras gráfica]]'' series ''[[The Life and Times of Xabier Cabaleiro]]'' as well as the introduction of [[Xoel Salgado]] in the years leading up to the [[Mauritius 1966 Summer Games]]. [[File:1000000th_Beetle.jpg|thumb|250px|The Golden Hayashi Mark One, manufactured to celebrate the fiftieth anniversary of the Hayashi Mark One in 1982.]]
[[Castadilla]] boasts one of the oldest and most competitive automotive industries in the world, having had its start in the late 1880s, as well as one of the most prominent and largest automotive industries. Since the end of the [[Second Great War]] in 1943, Castadilla has consistently been in the top three of the most productive automobile manufacturing industries with no less than 10 million cars being manufactured in the country annually. Production has grown even further as the nation's largest automotive firms have invested heavily into setting up automotive manufacturing plants in other countries, particularly to manufacture regional variants of existing models; [[Thervala]], for instance, is the primary manufacturing hub for Castadillaan brand automobiles in [[Audonia]].

articles.title: Cannabis_in_Castadilla
articles.snippet:
'''Cannabis in Castadilla''' is legal for {{wp|Cannabis (drug)|recreational}}, {{wp|Medical cannabis|medicinal}}, and commercial purposes, which was the result of the ''[[Cannabis Regulation Act (Castadilla)|Cannabis Regulation Act]]'' which was put into effect on 20 April 1930. Although there were other countries in which cannabis was legal, these were due to cannabis having never been criminalised in the first place; the passing of the ''Cannabis Regulation Act'' was one of the first times in which cannabis was made explicitly legal rather than merely implicitly legal.

The legalisation of cannabis was the result of a spontaneous {{wp|grassroots}} movement which had emerged in 1927 known as the [[Society for the Liberation of Psychoactives]] (SOLIPS). articles.title: Castadillaan_heraldry
articles.snippet:
'''Castadillaan heraldry''' is the use of {{wp|heraldry|heraldic}} symbols in [[Castadilla]]. Although initially very primitive, the first signs of recognisable heraldry could be found in the [[11th Century]], the result of [[Caphiria|Caphiric]] influence in [[Vallos]]. As a result, the earliest instances of heraldry in the subcontinent had a distinct Latinic aesthetic to it. Such a formality remains in use in Castadilla in both regulated personal heraldry as well as {{wp|Civic heraldry}} in daily life.

The role of the herald in Castadilla, as established in 1852, still exists to this day, and as such arms are regulated and granted to individual by the Castadillaan kings of arms of the [[Imperial Collegiate of Arms]]. This article serves as an overview for the '''cities of [[Castadilla]]''', or settlements of at least 50,000 inhabitants. The cities listed here will start off with the fifty largest cities in the country as per the [[2036 Castadilla census|2036 census]]. All cities listed are coterminous with urban or mixed municipalities, meaning that each are governed by a civic council headed by a ''señor de la cidade'' ("lord of the city"), and none span across more than one municipality. This also means that amalgamations can increase, shrink, or even subsume a municipality based on changing demographics and perceived belonging to a given city. There are also cities that, despite being surrounded by another city, have remained as separate cities due to their inhabitants being opposed to amalgamation; these types of cities are often known as ''illas terrestres'' or "land islands".

'''Citizenship law in Castadilla''' is a series of laws which determine who gets conferred Castadillaan nationality and who gets conferred Castadillaan citizenship. In [[Castadilla]], nationality and citizenship are both seen as two separate but interconnected legal concepts with the former often being referred to as the basic levels of citizenship in most other nations while the latter refers to the rights that are conferred to a citizen upon reaching the {{wp|age of majority}}.

The '''{{wp|coronation}} of the [[Castadillaan Emperor]]''' is a formal ceremony in which the Emperor is formally invested with the [[Imperial Crown of Castadilla|imperial regalia]] and is crowned at the [[Primatial Basilica of Las Joquis]]. It takes inspiration from coronations that have been historically performed in other monarchies in the [[Occidental]], with many traditions dating back to the middle ages, as well as the traditions maintained in [[Caphiria]] for their [[Coronation of the Imperator|imperial coronations]]. articles.title: Cuisine_of_Castadilla
articles.snippet: '''Castadillaan cuisine''' consists of the cooking traditions and practices within [[Castadilla]]. It principally derives from a mixing of [[Vallosi cuisine]], [[Sarpic cuisine]], [[Latinic cuisine]], [[Tainean cuisine]], [[Loa cuisine]], [[Samalosian cuisine]], [[Audonian cuisine]], and [[Homberto cuisine|''Homberto'' cuisine]]. Each major region in the country all have distinctive culinary elements, reflecting not only local food resources, local demographics, and local innovation. These developments have also given some states and cities their own distinctive culinary elements. For example, [[Navidadian cuisine]] reflects substantial Latinic and Loa influences, while the cuisine of [[Samalosi]] integrates not only Samalosian cuisine but also [[Cuisine of Daxia|Daxian]]. Proximity and territorial expansion have resulted in substantial influences from [[Cuisine of Cartadania|Cartadanian]] and [[Cuisine of Caphiria|Caphiric cuisines]]. articles.title: Delepasian_Centennial
articles.snippet:
{{WIP}}
The '''Delepasian Centennial''' was a yearlong celebration held in 1952 to celebrate the 100th anniversary of Delepasian independence. Celebrations in [[Estado Social (Castadilla)|Delepasia]] occurred throughout the year but the biggest celebrations culminated on [[Abjuration Day]], 30 April. Centennial celebrations meant that special, commemorative coins were minted that depicted various national symbols, such as the [[Militiaman]], on the reverse. Communities and organisations across the country were encouraged to engage in Centennial projects and events in celebration of the anniversary. These projects could range from one-time events to local improvement projects whether it be municipal arenas or parks. The fountain at the [[Capitolium of Castadilla|Capitolium]] was replaced with a new fountain with an {{wp|eternal flame}} in the middle. Any children born in 1952 were declared Centennial babies.

articles.title: Delepasian_Diaspora
articles.snippet:
{{MajorReconstruction}}

The '''Delepasian Diaspora''' refers to the demographics of [[Delepasians]] living abroad outside the sovereign borders of [[Castadilla]]. Delepasians live abroad for a variety of reasons, usually these are permanent residents in other Cronan countries, Delepasian members of the Castadillaan business community working for respective private and public enterprises, non-governmental organization workers such as doctors and humanitarian aid workers, or Delepasians on official Castadillaan business such as diplomatic missions.

The Delepasian diaspora is most prominently found in [[Crona]] and mainland [[Sarpedon]], however there is significant Delepasian presence in friendly nations or those with cultural ties, such as [[Lucrecia]] or [[Cartadania]]. There are approximately 24,000,000 Delepasians living abroad as of 2040, with that number expected to grow by 2050.

articles.title: Delepasian_exceptionalism
articles.snippet:
'''Delepasian exceptionalism''' is the belief that the [[Delepasians|Delepasian]] people are the ordained hegemons of [[Vallos]] based on the principle of divine right and that they may achieve this role through key values which make the Delepasians great. Proponents of this belief have argued that through {{wp|ultranationalism}}, {{wp|traditionalist Catholicism}}, and {{wp|integralism}}, the Delepasian people would be destined for to become the predominant culture in Vallos. It was the main ideological component of the ''[[Estado Social (Castadilla)|Estado Social]]'' regime and its ruling [[National Renewal Party]] from 1924 until the regime's collapse to the [[Velvet Revolution]] in 1984.

The term had emerged in the 1840s to refer to the long history of {{wp|constitutionalism}} and {{wp|autonomy}} held by the [[Viceroyalty of Los Rumas]] and how the colonists have long seen themselves as distinct cultures from the main [[Pelaxians|Pelaxian]] culture. articles.title: Delepasianism
articles.snippet:
'''Delepasianism''', or '''Delepasian Idealism''', is an 18th-19th Century philosophical and political movement based on the ideas of the [[Kilikas Enlightenment]] as well as the ideas of author and triumvir of the [[First Pelaxian Republic]] [[Luciano Valera]]. The primary characteristic of Delepasianism is the {{wp|dialectic|dialectical method}} which supposes that the internal contradictions within given concepts can mobilise the development of the ''Espirito'' ("Spirit") throughout history before ultimately culminating in the ''Espirito''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s own self-realisation and rational unfolding into reality.

Delepasianists believe that the conceptual ideal is not only subjective, but that it serves as a fundamental aspect of objectivity. They also believe in a {{wp|constitution|constitutional}} form of government governed by the {{wp|rule of law}} with {{wp|democracy|democratic}} and {{wp|meritocracy|meritocratic}} principles. articles.title: Healthcare_in_Castadilla
articles.snippet: '''Healthcare in Castadilla''' is, according to the [[Constitution of Castadilla|constitution]], almost exclusively under the ownership of the government and is one of the sectors of the economy in which private firms are barred from directly competing in with the sole exceptions being facilities owned and operated by the [[Catholic Apostolic Church]] and charitable organisations. As such, [[Castadilla]]'s healthcare system is a {{wp|Single-payer healthcare|single-payer system}}; all healthcare resources and personnel are owned and employed by the government-run [[Imperial Healthcare System]] which itself is administered by the [[Minister of Health (Castadilla)|Ministry of Health]]. As a {{wp|federal state}}, the day-to-day operation of hospitals and maintenance in Castadilla are overseen by the individual [[Administrative divisions of Castadilla|states]]. articles.title: History_of_Castadilla
articles.snippet:
The '''history of Castadilla''' goes back to a few millennia ago and spans from the emergence of the [[Vallosi people|indigenous Vallosi]] [[Glaistic civilization|Glaistic civilisation]] all the way to the present. The lands of what are now a part of Castadilla, excluding overseas territories, were inhabited for millennia by not only the indigenous Vallosi people, but also the Polynesians, who are now the [[Loa]], the [[Taineans]], who came from [[Crona]] via the [[Heaven Ships]], and the [[Latinic people|Latins]], who were settlers from the [[Adonerum]]. All four groups have had their own cultures, traditions, religious beliefs, and even various forms of government. Of the four groups, however, the indigenous Vallosi have long since faded by the end of the colonial era in the mid-19th Century with their existences only being proven through archeological artifacts and genealogical studies.

articles.snippet:
[[File:Castadillaan Housing.jpg|thumb|500px|Various types of housing in Castadilla.]]
'''Housing in Castadilla''' refers to the economic sector in [[Castadilla]] pertaining to {{wp|real estate}} and {{wp|housing tenure}}. Throughout Castadilla's history, and that of [[Vallos]] in general, there were many different types of housing styles and housing tenures depending on the culture and social status of a given person. Modern Castadillaan housing styles and housing tenures are derived from the housing styles and tensures found throughout the [[Occident]] and come in a wide range of architectural styles depending on the culture and building materials found in a given area as well as the specific purpose of a given household being built.

articles.title: Industrialisation_of_Castadilla
Internet_in_Castadilla
articles.snippet:
'''Internet in Castadilla''', or '''Castadillaan Internet''' ([[Castadillaan Pelaxian|Pelaxian]]: ''Intrede en Castadiłano''), and sometimes referred to as '''[[Castanet]]''' (a {{wp|portmanteau}} of "Castadillaan" and "Internet"; Pelaxian: ''Castarede''), is the part of the {{wp|Internet}} that is related to [[Castadilla]]. As of 2013, Internet access in Castadilla is available to both business and home users in various methods and forms, such as {{wp|Dial-up Internet access|dial-up}}, {{wp|DOCSIS|cable}}, {{wp|Digital subscriber line|DSL}}, {{wp|Fiber to the x|FTTH}}, mobile, {{wp|Wireless Internet|wireless}}, and {{wp|Satellite Internet access|satellite}}.

As of 2040, 98% of the country's total population, or 236,308,448 [[Castadillaans]], were Internet users. In that same year, Castadilla has ranked highly amongst the world's countries with regards to the average {{wp|broadband|fixed broadband}} {{wp|Internet access}} {{wp|Data signaling rate|speed}}; download speed in Castadilla

articles.title: Isurian_revivalism
articles.snippet:
[[File:Three-crosses-on-a-hill_-_West_Virginia_-_ForestWander.jpg|thumb|330px|[[Calvary (monument)|Calvaries]] are one of the most well-known symbols of Isurian revivalism.]]
'''Isurian revivalism''' is a series of cultural phenomena that have emerged during the latter half of the 19th Century which was prevalent throughout both [[Lucrecia]] and [[Delepasian Confederation|Delepasia]] (now [[Castadilla]]) which have renewed interest in the [[Isurians]] and their culture. It has often been cited as having had wide-ranging effects on not only Castadillaan and Lucrecian history, but also on the overall evolution of the [[Vallos|Vallosi]] vernaculars of the [[Pelaxian language]] in mainland Vallos and the eventual rise of [[Isurianism]] in Lucrecian politics as well as the rise of [[Delepasian exceptionalism]] in [[Delepasians|Delepasian]] culture. The exact dates for when Isurian revivalism began and when it ended are subject to debate, and may very well diverge depending on the country;

articles.snippet:
This article lists '''{{wp|political parties}} in [[Castadilla]]'''. The Castadillaan political scene has been dominated by the [[People's Democratic Party]] ever since the end of the 1984 [[Velvet Revolution]], although the [[Christian National Party (Castadilla)|Christian National Party]], alongside the [[Democratic Reform Party (Castadilla)|Democratic Reform Party]], the [[Castadillaan Citizens' Party]], and others have managed to maintain a presence in some regional and local governments.

articles.title: Loa_Laws
articles.snippet:
The '''Loa Laws''' ([[Pelaxian language|Pelaxian]]: ''Leis Loa'') refer to the set of laws enacted in [[Navidadia]] with the express purpose of discriminating against the [[Loa people|Loa]] which carried into the [[Delepasian Commonwealth]]. These laws served as the legal backbone of the [[Navidadian System]], especially the laws passed after the [[United Navidadian Party]] won its first government in 1940, which were the brainchild of the racial theory written by [[Pablo Rosales]], who became Minister of Loa Affairs in 1945 and President of Navidadia in 1953.

The basis behind these laws came to be around the time of Navidadia's establishment in 1875 when the nation's first president, [[Sancho Abascal]], explained that "the sheer incivility and cruelty of the Loa against our forefathers the Romany is clear indication that our society has no need nor want of these savages; they are to be shown how to behave properly, how to live like normal civilised human beings lest they wish to beco

articles.snippet: The '''Navidadian System''' ([[Pelaxian language|Pelaxian]]: ''Sistema Navidadiano'') was a system of institutionalised {{wp|racial segregation}} that existed in the Delepasian ''[[Estado Social (Castadilla)|Estado Social]]'' regime from 1943 until it was dismantled after the [[Velvet Revolution]] of 1984, though its dissolution would not be made official until 1995. The Navidadian System was characterised by an authoritarian political culture based on ''{{wp|baasskap|democracia jefatura}}'' (boss-hood democracy), which ensured that Delepasia, was dominated politically, socially, and economically by the nation's [[Delepasians]]. In this supremacist system, there was {{wp|social stratification}}, where [[Delepasians]], [[Pelaxians]] and [[Cartadanians]] had the highest status, followed by [[Taineans]], the [[Samalosi people|Samalosi]], then the [[Loa]]. articles.snippet:
{{NonCanon}}
[[File:Wine cellar.jpg|thumb|right|A traditional wine cellar in a Valariano vineyard.]]
[[Aciria]] has a long history of winemaking. The warm weather paired with the vast flatlands of Valariano and protective valleys in the Montanaro region located in southern Valariano and Santa Beatrice have enabled Acirian wine production since at least 3000 BC. The wines produced today are mainly expensive luxury wines meant for export to foreign markets, but many more affordable wines are also produced for domestic Acirian markets. Due to the long history of wine and its close association with Acirian history, culture and people, the drink is seen as inseparable from the national identity of Aciria.

articles.title: Architecture_in_Daxia
articles.snippet:
Daxian architecture encompasses a series of styles that have been prevalent through various historical eras. Invasions and intermixing with other races has added certain diversity of style to various geographical areas such as the west and far north of the country.
==Imperial Style==
The architectural style of Daxia during the dynastic period developed for hundreds of years, with many structural principles remaining the same even after a new dynasty took over. Symmetry, the use of enclosed open spaces such as courtyards and inner gardens and the addition of figures from Daxian myth in the decorative details are notable characteristics of the Imperial style.

articles.title: Association_for_the_Defense_of_the_Taizi_Sea
articles.snippet:
The '''Association for the Defense of the Taizi Sea''' is a civil organization whose main objective is the renaming of the internationally known 'Pukthun Sea' to the traditional Daxian name, the Taizi Sea. They routinely hold rallies and protests at the League of Nations headquarters in [[Alba Concordia]] and at Pukhtunkhwa's embassy building in [[Mirzak]]. They also operate a small fleet of ships that they use to harass and intimidate Pukhtun fishing boats in international waters. Other stunts include using improvised catapults to bombard Pukhtun businesses with pork leftovers.

articles.title: Avidor_Boruch
articles.snippet:
[[File:南公懷仁像.jpg|thumb|A Qian period image of Avidor Boruch during his time as Chief Astronomer of the Imperial Court.]]
'''Avidor Boruch''' also known as '''Wang Ming''' (1582-1665) was a [[Zorfashazi]] Jew who served the [[Daxia|Qian dynasty]] as is best known for being the court's Chief Astronomer under emperors [[Dizong]] and [[Baizou]]. He also founded and served as first director of the Imperial Observatory for forty years. His service as an imperial advisor spanned the reign of three different emperors, of which he personally tutored two. The discovery of the [[Kalgan]] planetoid is attributed to him.

He was the first Jew in Qian service to officially be granted a bureaucrat's hat and robe. He became one of the most renowned Jews in service to a [[Daxia]]n dynasty, many who followed him would play important roles in the development of various scientific fields.

The '''Captivity of Weeping Sores''' as the Chimor people call it, also known as the '''Golden Refuge''' in official [[Daxia]]n sources refers to the captivity of the entire [[Chimoche]] royal family from 1714 to 2015 by [[Daxia]]. After [[Chimoche]]'s defeat in the Second Qian-Chimor war, king Tizroc V was captured alongside with all of his family and escorted into captivity at the [[Pinghai]] fortress. Tizroc V and his family would spend the next fifteen years there in cramped accommodation. Upon Tizroc's death in 1729, his successor Tizroc VI and the rest of the royal clan would be moved to mainland [[Daxia]]. They were then escorted overland to the Blue Tile Palace (''Daxian:Lanse Cízhuān'') in northern [[Daxia]] which would be the clan's permanent abode for the next 287 years. articles.title: Chen's_Menagerie
articles.snippet:
The '''Mirzak Institute for Biological Preservation''', known more widely as '''Chen's Menagerie''' after former Chancellor [[Linge Chen]] is a biological reserve and research institute in [[Daxia]]. Originally a zoological garden created for the enjoyment of Chen himself, it was repurposed after his death. It now houses hundreds of animal specimens from all over the world along with local fauna and hosts an unknown number of labs, many below ground level.
[[File:Menagerie.jpg|thumb|Aerial view of Chen's Menagerie]]
==History==
Built in 1998 in the western outskirts of [[Mirzak]], the original menagerie was initially meant to house Linge Chen's two [[Long-toothed Hound]]s Toramino and Berossus. While it is rumored that Chen may have on occasion fed some of his political opponents to his pets, he also ordered that the compound be equipped with state of the art cattle and poultry farms to provide meat for his animals. articles.title: Chongbai
articles.snippet: '''Chongbai''' (崇拜) also called '''Worship of the Deep''' is the ethnic religion of [[Daxia]] and is practiced by a majority of the [[Daxian people]]. A polytheistic religion, the Chongbai pantheon is composed of dozens of gods and hundreds of minor deities and aspects of nature. Aspects of Chongbai have influenced the cosmovision of [[Daxian people|Daxians]] and their sense of [[Zhangwo|special destiny]]; [[Daxia]]n racialist theories are deeply enmeshed with Chongbai religious doctrines. The Emperors were considered to be the heads of the Chongbai religious hierarchy thanks to their special connections to the divine, in their absence the Custodian of the Grand Temple of Diqiu and Grand Hierophant is considered the seniormost and preeminent religious figure. Out of favor after the end of dynastic rule, Chongbai has begun to see a revival in its popularity during the last two decades as resistance and agitation against 'foreign' religions is on the rise. articles.title: Culture_of_Daxia
articles.snippet:
[[File:Consort_Rong_dressed_in_Manchu_Clothes.JPG|thumb|Portrait of Empress Weiziao, an example of 18th century Qian oil painting]]
The '''culture of Daxia''' has been historically shaped by its lengthy periods of insularity, even from other cultures in [[Audonia]]. When a state of internal order and peace was prevalent, successive [[Daxia]]n empires would slowly seek to impose their own cultural mores on neighboring states, often through force of arms. articles.title: Daxian_Aspic
articles.snippet:
'''Daxian Aspic''' is a food dish in which varied ingredients are set into gelatin, usually made from commercial gelatin mixes. Most types of food can be used for Aspic dishes such as meat, vegetables fruits and even fish. The origin of [[Daxia]]'s aspic food is its prison system but it has spread to the lower echelons of society hence it is disdainfully called 'trash food' by the upper classes.

==Origins==
The invention of the greatly reviled aspic is attributed to Qiao Yun, Vice Warden of [[Mirzak]]'s central prison. Following the Party's 1995 directive to bring down incarceration costs, he sought a way to save on food consumption and make prisoners more compliant by reducing their caloric intake. He found the solution in one of his favorite desserts, jello. By combining the power and versatility of powdered gelatin with other food, visually appealing and stomach filling dishes could be created. articles.title: Drug_trade_in_Daxia
articles.snippet:
[[File:Captagon pills.png|thumb|Captagon pills produced in [[Daxia]]]]
The '''drug trade in [[Daxia]]''' is an activity that goes back centuries to the Zhong dynasty. Belying its status as a harsh and unforgiving police state, numerous drugs and addictive substances are actually legal to manufacture, sell and consume in the [[Daxia|Repubic of Daxia]]. The nation is the world's top producer of opiates, crystal methamphetamine and captagon. Giant pharmaceutical conglomerates such as the [[Opodo Corporation]] and [[Samgor]] produce and market hundreds of tons of addictive substances every year, officially solely for internal consumption, but in all likelihood also for export by international trafficking networks with links to government figures.

articles.title: Dwarfism_in_Daxia
articles.snippet:
[[File:Elder Dwarves.jpg|thumb|Elderly Daxian dwarves]]
In ancient [[Daxia]] dwarves and pygmies were seen as people that had been cursed by deities at birth or whose parents were being punished for some transgression. These beliefs led dwarves to be shunned or exiled from their communities at best and persecuted or killed at worst. Ancient [[Daxia]]n religions sometimes made use of dwarves in rituals, and many times the dwarves did not make it out unscathed. There are ancient records that document attempts to cure dwarfism by officials. These attempts included rearranging a dwarves organs as it was believed the limbs had shriveled due to poor blood circulation and moving bigger organs to the chest would somehow remedy this.

Daxian oficial policy as communicated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs is to pursue positive and beneficial relations with all states, with the goal of guaranteeing Daxian independence, sovereignty, territorial integrity and creating a favorable international atmosphere in which to further its economic and geopostrategic interests.

'''Good Barbarians '''or '''Guoyi''' was an official term used by successive [[Daxia]]n dynasties to refer to outside peoples who paid tribute but were considered to have no true civilization as the Daxians understood it. Classical studies of Imperial [[Daxia]] and its interactions with foreigners by western historians tended to think that [[Daxia]]n imperial authorities classified all outsiders under the same category of barbarians but more recently discovered imperial historical records and translations of scholarly texts from the Zhong dynasty onwards make clear the distinction of the Guoyi from other foreigners. Some recently recovered [[Imperial Tallies (Daxia)|imperial tallies]] include the term alongside the names of Kochok Khan and Desai Khan, the twelfth and sixteenth rulers respectivelly of the [[Degei Confederation]] who were known to be vassals of the Zhong dynasty. articles.title: Great_Arsenal
articles.snippet:
[[File:Japanese_battleship_Mikasa.jpg|thumb|Battleship ''Tiequan'', flagship of the [[Harmonious Flotilla Invincible]] during the early 1900's. The battleship was one of thirty commissioned by the navy during this period.]]
The '''Great Arsenal''' (大炮) is the name colloquialy given to the modernized armed forces of the [[Daxia|Qian dynasty]] during the 18th and 19th centuries. The impetus for the creation of the Great Arsenal was the Truce of Caserges signed in 1728 that ended the [[Daxian Polynesian Wars]], Daxia's failure to achieve its objectives during the conflict led the imperial court to conclude that its forces were increasingly inadequate to face all its competitors. Beginning in the mid 18th century the Qian state poured vast resources into both the development of new weaponry and the theft and copying of foreign designs. [[File:Portrait_of_Eliezer_Ben-Yehuda_(cropped).jpg|thumb|[[Adolph Goldberg]], an adherent to ''doikayt'' ("hereness"), was the main founder of the modern New Eshelist movement. He envisioned [[Delepasian Confederation|Delepasia]] (now [[Castadilla]]) as the new {{wp|Jewish homeland}}.]]
'''New Eshelism''' ({{wp|Hebrew language|Hebrew}}: הטשאלות החדשה, {{small|{{wp|Romanization of Hebrew|romanised}}}}: ''HatEshaelot HaChadsha'') is a political ideology in [[Castadilla]] that deems the Castadillaan state to be the new {{wp|Jewish homeland}} in of itself on the basis of the nation having long been a Jewish safe haven. It is the main ideology of the [[Jewish Consolidation Front]] (הַלִּיכּוּד, ''Likud''), the oldest continuously-existing [[List of political parties in Castadilla|political party in Castadilla]], and comes in many political and ideological variations. It is the main political movement of the [[Jews in Castadilla|Judeo-Delepasians]].

'''RIIC''', short for '''''Rede Imperial de Informaxón Computaxonal''''' ({{Literal translation|Imperial Network for Computational Information}}), is the automated [[Economy of Castadilla|national economy]] manager for [[Castadilla]]. The RIIC project began in 1964 during the ''[[Estado Social (Castadilla)|Estado Social]]'' era and has had its basis in successful experiements in early {{wp|ternary computer|ternary computer systems}} in the 1950s, but it was not until the establishment of the [[Unified Communications Network]] within the [[Videocom|Televideo]] network in the late 1970s that the project would begin to be seriously implemented as a distributed {{wp|decision support system}}. articles.title: Social_media_in_Castadilla
articles.snippet:
'''Social media in Castadilla''' developed early on in the history of modern telecommunications in the country with the first online network being [[Videocom|Televideo]] which was a {{wp|videotex}} service which pre-dated the Internet as well as the {{wp|World Wide Web}} and relied on telephone lines. This included a primitive social messaging system known as the [[Unified Communications Network]] which was a {{wp|bulletin board system}} and was initially designed to share information and resources between economic institutions; the idea was to create a distributed {{wp|decision support system}} which would assist in economic management. However, although the project was not discontinued, the Unified Communications Network soon became a way to send messages on an unmediated platform and thus was used for want ads, sharing media, engaging in idle chatter, and even to post what were considered to be the precursor to {{wp|blog|blogs}}.

articles.title: Taxation_in_Castadilla
articles.snippet:
'''Taxation in Castadilla''' refers to the system of {{wp|tax|taxes}} levied by the [[Magisterial Council of Castadilla|federal government]], by the [[Administrative divisions of Castadilla#States|state]] governments, and by the [[Local government in Castadilla|local governments]]. The exact taxes levied depends on the level of government, but the three major sources of taxation are {{wp|Value-added tax|value-added taxes}}, {{wp|Corporate tax|corporate income taxes}}, {{wp|sales tax|sales taxes}}, and {{wp|Income tax|personal income taxes}}.

The [[Imperial Revenue Agency]] administers the collection of federal and state taxes where it then remits the states' shares to the relevant states based on their tax contributions in a given year; each state is remitted state personal income taxes, corporate taxes, and portions of the [[Cumulative Sales Tax]] in excess of the federal [[Imperial Consumption Tax]] rate of 7%.

articles.title: Television_in_Castadilla
articles.snippet: '''Television in Castadilla''' began in 1933 with one of the first regular television services in the world. The ''[[Castadillaan Broadcasting Corporation|Servizo de Televixón Imperial]]'' ("Imperial Television Service") entered regular service on 17 September 1933 after a two-year experimental phase and was an exclusively {{wp|public service}}. The broadcasting schedule was initially limited to a half-hour for every broadcast day, a limit which was particularly strict during the [[Second Great War]]. It would not be until the latter years of the Second Great War that the service's broadcasting schedule would be expanded, allowing for three hours to be broadcasted four times a week. As of 2039, the three biggest television networks are the state-run [[Castadillaan Broadcasting Corporation]] (CCR), the publicly funded nonprofit [[Imperial Broadcasting Network]] (RRI), and the privately-owned [[Celovision]]. '''''Tiras gráficas''''', [[Castadillaan Pelaxian|Pelaxian]] for 'graphic strips' and abbreviated as '''TGs''', also referred to as '''Delepasian comics''', is a term used to refer to {{wp|comics}} made in [[Delepasia]] and [[Castadilla]] and written in the country's variety of the [[Pelaxian language]]. Castadilla, and the preceding Delepasia, has had a long and established tradition in both comics and drawn cartoons which has emerged independently of the traditions found in [[Levantia]], [[Alstin]], and [[Asteria]]. articles.title: Titles_of_the_Castadillaan_Imperial_Family
articles.snippet:
The '''titles of the Castadillaan Imperial Family''' forms a legal system comprising the {{wp|hereditary title|hereditary titles}} associated with the [[Castadillaan Imperial Family|Imperial Family]], composed of several {{wp|Imperial, royal and noble ranks|ranks}}, and within the framework of the [[Constitution of Castadilla]] form a constituent part of the [[Imperial Households of Castadilla|Imperial Households]] and of the nation's [[Orders of precedence in Castadilla|orders of precedence]]. These titles determine the position of a member of the imperial family in relation to their seniority. Although some of these titles might make it seem like the members of the Imperial Family are a part of the [[Peerage in Castadilla|nation's peerage]], this is not necessarily the case as members of the Imperial Family are considered to be ranking above the peerage and thus are not allowed to run for office in the [[Congress of the Peerage]] so as to avoid conflicts of interest.

articles.title: Western_Imperium
articles.snippet: The '''Western Imperium''' is a hypothesised geopolitical concept used to describe non-[[Caphiria|Caphirian]] nations that have sought to or have held a hegemony over the subcontinent of [[Vallos]] which is located to the west of mainland [[Sarpedon]], with the "Eastern Imperium" exclusively referring to Caphiria due to its long-held status of being the hegemon of mainland Sarpedon. Historically, there have been three nations which have been considered to have been the "Western Imperium", those being [[Kingdom of Septemontes|Septemontes]] and [[Kingdom of Oduria|Oduria]] during the [[Second Vallosi Warring States period|post-Undecimvirate]] era, and [[Pelaxia]] during its zenith in the [[Carto-Pelaxian Commonwealth|Commonwealth]] era. The term is mostly used to describe nations that were considered to be the predominant great power in Vallos, particularly nations that were historically in opposition to the "Eastern Imperium". The '''1993 Tierradorian financial crisis''' was a severe [[w:Financial crisis|economic crisis]] which began in mid-to-late 1993 and went on until 1996, where it affected several [[Crona|South Cronan]] nations, most notably [[Tierrador]]. The collapse of the [[1985–1993 Tierradorian housing bubble|housing bubble]] in Tierrador and [[Ceylonia]], [[w:Predatory lending|various predatory lending groups]] taking advantage of low and middle income homebuyers and homeowners within the countries, and ridiculously excessive risk-taking by Tierradorian [[w:Financial institution|financial institutions]], which resulted in [[w:Bank runs|bank runs]], [[w:Default (finance)|bank defaults]], and the closing, acquisition, and/or bankruptcy of several medium and large financial institutions throughout Tierrador.

articles.title: Culture_of_Drasenia
articles.snippet:
[[File:Entrada da Livraria Lello.jpg|thumb|The National Library of Tóroqua|border]]
Even as the culture of [[Drasenia]] shares several characteristics with that of the Istroyo-Adonerii culture group of the [[Occidental world]], it nonetheless displays several unique traits, due to the heavy influence of medieval communalism and Polynesian culture over the country; Latin views on justice and violence and Polynesian views on nudity and sexuality coexist in the nation, whose inhabitants tend to be duty-bound and honour-bound in the public sphere, and carefree and relaxed, open and honest in the private sphere. articles.title: Energy_in_Kiravia
articles.snippet:
[[File:Shatura steam power plant (2010).jpg|thumb|Peat-fired power plant in [[Intravia|Intravia State]]. Kiravia is the leading consumer of {{wp|peat}} as fuel, and the largest consumer of biomass fuel among developed nations.]]

Kiravia is the largest energy consumer in Ixnay and the leading energy importer. Although Kiravia is decently endowed with conventional energy resources, the vast energy demand generated by its large population, advanced economy, and cool climate greatly outstrip domestic supply. Maintaining a reliable energy supply and reasonable prices is a perennial policy concern at the federal level, and a great deal of public expenditure has been dedicated to energy subsidies, energy research, the development of domestic energy sources, and the upkeep of good trade relations with major energy-exporting countries, such as [[Cartadania]] and [[Arcerion]].

articles.title: Great_Depression
articles.snippet:
{{wip}}

The '''Great Depression''' was a severe worldwide economic depression that took place mostly during the 1910s-1930s. The timing of the Great Depression varied across nations; in most countries, it started in the early 1910s and lasted until the early 1930s. The Great Depression is commonly used as an example of how intensely the world's economy can decline.
==Background==
During the [[Red Interregnum]], southern [[Levantia]] faced a series of economic crisis. The fear of a socialist [[Urcea]] lead to market crashes in most capitalist nations across the globe, but the quick restoration of the monarchy ended the Depression of [[1900]] and most markets bounced back. The fairly new [[Burgundie|Burgoignesc]] gens des mejans tried to profit off of the war and the Depression of [[1900]]. articles.title: Grog_Fleet
articles.snippet:
[[File:GrogFleet.jpg|thumb|Vessels of the Grog Fleet]]
The Grog Fleet was a [[Daxia]]n naval convoy system operating from the Daxian mainland to the island of [[Zhijun]] on [[Australis]], the purpose of which was the procurement and transport of rum which was made with sugar cane from Zhijun's abundant sugar cane plantations. The Qian Court were great consumers of rum and having no local conditions for the growth of rum's main ingredient, it had to be transported on enormous cargo ships dubbed 'Grog Ships' which could fit hundreds of barrels in their holds. Sailors were given an allowance of watered down rum to consume during the trips, hence the name Grog Fleet, but no actual grog was transported to [[Daxia]].

articles.title: History_of_Drasenia
articles.snippet:
{{Award winning article}}
The '''history of Drasenia''' goes as far back as 12,000 BC, when - just like the rest of [[Vallos]] - [[Drasenia]] was first inhabited by the peoples that eventually established the [[Glaistic civilization]]; these first inhabitants were then absorbed by the ancestors of the Tangata Lua - by 600 AD, when the whole of Vallos fell under [[Caphiria]]'s control, they too had largely fused with the descendants of [[Adonerum|Adonerii]] colonists, refugees and traders. articles.title: Imperial_Lemon_Grove
articles.snippet:
[[File:Grove Fountain.jpg|thumb|An artistic rendition of the southern fountain in the Imperial Lemon Grove.]]
The '''Imperial Lemon Grove''' was a large grove of lemon trees located within the [[Palace of Columns]] near the summer imperial capital of [[Daguo]], [[Daxia]]. The first trees were uprooted from [[Rusana]] and planted in the grove by Emperor Chengzi in the year 1256 to provide lemons for his predilection for drinking a glass of lemonade every day. The incorporation of parts of [[Rusana]] later in history and the expansion of trade meant the grove was more decorative and recreational in nature later on. During Chengzi's reign the grove grew to cover an area of sixty hectares and included walkways, artificial ponds housing exotic fish such as giant carp, bridges, a pagoda and several carved gazebos where palace visitors and officials could meet for lunch.

articles.title: Lake_Zhenzhu
articles.snippet:
[[File:Baotou.jpg|thumb|Lake Zhenzhu on a good day]]
Lake Zhenzhu is the largest man-made toxic sludge lake in the world. Located outside [[Minxia City]], it is fed by pipes from dozens of steel mills that dump toxic residue in it. Described as 'the pride of [[Minxia City]]' it is a major tourist attraction, its waters are however anathema to all life. 
Once a pristine lake home to a nesting ground for many migratory bird species, the declaration of a special program of industrial incentives for [[Minxia City]]  led to a massive boom in extractive and transformative industries. Steel mills, mineral refineries and processing plants sprouted like mushrooms, encouraged by city officials and lax enviromental protections. By the early 2010's the lake had been completely fouled by sludge that it was reclassified as a toxic body of water and swimming was prohibited. articles.title: Master_of_Tongues
articles.snippet:
[[File:Ronan Hill.jpg|thumb|Portrait of Ronan Hill, [[Urcean people|Urcean]]-born Master of Tongues to Emperor Tengu the Sot]]
The '''Master of Tongues''' (恶魔音箱) was the chief interpreter to the imperial court of [[Daxia]]. The position was first created during the Shang dynasty and persisted through the Chen, Zhong and Qian periods. The Master of Tongues was a very important functionary and was one of the chief aides to the ministers in charge of foreign affairs. In [[Daxia]]n idiosyncrasy the speaking of foreign tongues was considered disgraceful and unbecoming of a proper [[Daxia]]n, therefore the task of acting as interpreters fell to foreigners. These were usually former slaves bought, received as [[Tributary system of Imperial Daxia|tribute]] or captured from enemy territories. Most of the early royal interpreters were of Muslim origin due to the Chen dynasty's frequent interaction with former Oduniyyad polities and a handful of Muslim families monopolized the position for decade

articles.title: Mirzak_Cheese_Vaults
articles.snippet:
[[File:Cheese.jpg|thumb|Inside view of one the cheese vaults]]
The '''Mirzak Cheese Vaults''' are a secret underground facility in [[Mirzak]] that holds the [[Daxia]]n strategic cheese reserve. The government of [[Daxia]] as part of its food security policies maintains a cyclopean surplus of cheese that can be distributed to the public in case of a grave disruption of supply chains caused by general warfare and naval blockades. [[Daxia]]n cheeses made from the milk of the hardy [[Daxian donkey]] can also be preserved in storage for many years without any degrading of its quality or taste.

While the strategic cheese reserve has existed since the early 1970's, all of the product was bought from private conglomerates, known collectively as [[Big Cheese]]. [[Big Cheese]] dominated the cheese market and operated it as a racket, driving the prices to ludicrous levels by keeping most of the cheese stored away. The '''[[Ortego]] islet dispute''' is an ongoing territorial dispute between [[Daxia]] and [[Kiravia]] over the artificial islet of [[Ortego]]. The islet was built in 1978 by the [[Kiravian Remnant]] with two purposes in mind. Firstly as a possible bolthole for high ranking members of the [[Renaissance Party]] and secondly as a way to section off a large triangular area between the [[Orixtal Sea|Sea of Orixtal]] and the [[Polynesian Sea]] for oil exploration. The other two points of the triangle were to be [[Sarolasta]] and [[Seváronsa]]. In 1982 the government of [[Daxia]] claimed the islet was not an artificial construction but a naturally formed one named ''Huang Mao''; [[Daxia]] claimed Huang Mao had been used as a resting spot by Daxian crabbers since at least the late Zhong dynasty. [[File:Bamboo_book_-_binding_-_UCR.jpg|thumb|Bamboo stick version of the Book of Artifice]]
'''Qipian's Book of Artifice''' is a treatise on scams and chicanery written by the [[Daxia]]n eunuch Qipian, a famous bandit leader in the late Chen dynasty who is also known as the '''Sage of Thievery'''. Penned and distributed to his forces as a practical guide for raising money through illegal means, it would become a blueprint to follow for [[Daxia]]n criminal organizations long after the author's capture and execution. Qipian's band was behind one of the first pyramid schemes in history, taking money from investors in order to "''carry out an undertaking of great advantage''" that ended in the collapse of Qaxi's provincial economy.

'''Quince Diplomacy''' is the name of a strategy of international engagement and diplomacy used predominantly by [[Daxia]] during the years the country was ruled by the [[National Reconstruction Front (Daxia)|National Reconstruction Front]]. It entailed the wooing of foreign diplomats and dignitaries by gifting them with quince fruits.
