'''Homo sapiens sigmanesis''', known commonly as ''Sigma males'' are an extinct species or subspecies of archaic humans who lived in [[Sarpedon]] until about 40,000 years ago. Many scientists have posited that they are distant relatives of the [[Kikpari]]. They were characterized by large, protruding jaws and were thought to be over seven feet tall.

==Social behavior==

Sigmanesis was known, unlike humans, to be a non-social creature, with most children leaving their mother as soon as able to walk. Accordingly, many young sigmanesis were killed by wild animals, though those that survived often had advanced survival and hunting skills. '''Slingin' Seamus''' (born '''James Larcus'''; March 19, 1847 - September 1, 1882) was an outlaw and gunfighter of the [[Urcean frontier]]. Although famous in his own time for successfully robbing eighteen trains, he became more famous posthumously in the public imagination in his role as gunfighter, particularly for his rivalry with Marcus Enni and his last stand at Somerville, which became the template for gun duels in future Levantine media.

articles.title: Valerian_Sands
articles.snippet:
{{wip}}
'''Valerian Sands''' is a gated residential community in the city of [[New Venceia, Alexandria|New Venceia]], [[Alexandria]]. Located in the city's Sagittaria Beach district, the neighborhood spans {{convert|450|ha|acre}} along Alexandria's northeastern coastline. It was developed by [[QV Properties]] of [[Caphiria]] and is the most expensive neighborhood in [[Cartadania]], with homes often selling for at least [[Escudo|€]]8 million. Due to upscale nature of the Sagittaria Beach district as a whole, the area often sees a lot of tourism, both domestic and international, and Valerian Sands is often the subject and setting of media and some films.

articles.title: Varshani_caste_system
articles.snippet:
{{wip}}

The '''Varshani caste system''' was one of the most important institutions within [[Culture of Varshan|Varshani culture]] during the [[Zurgite Varshan|Zurgite period]] of Varshani history. [[Orthodox Arzalism]] prescribed a hierarchical society that divides the population into castes according to their race, occupation, and relationship to the means of production in a [[Slavery in Varshan|slave-based economy]]. 

Varshanis of divine descent > TopVarshani priests > TopVarshani warriors > Petty Varshani priests > Petty Varshani Warriors > Top Varshani non-warriors > Petty Varshani non-warriors > Martial among Gentiles warriors > Martial among Gentiles non-warriors > "Natives" (Varshani Natives > Non-Varshani natives) > Varshani slaves > Non-Varshani slaves

articles.title: Varshani_historiography
articles.snippet:
The [[History of Varshan]] is largely based on records, stories, epics, and sagas retained in the cultural memory and archives of Varshan. Many problems exist with recounting the history of Varshan. It is consistently characterized by inconsistencies, especially chronological problems that often put dynasties existing at overlapping periods where none exist at a sequentially earlier part. [[Occidental]] historians and scholars, given access to all Varshani records and archives after the [[Final War of the Deluge]], have been actively working to construct concise, legible histories of Varshan for global use; this process has run into significant difficulties due to the many historiographical issues encountered.

articles.title: Augustus_(Great_Levantia)
articles.snippet:
{{Urcea WIP}}

The title of '''Augustus''' is used to refer to the {{Wp|paramount leader}} of [[Great Levantia]] between the reign of [[Gaius Stephanus Pictor]] and the end of the state in [[502]] AD. 

The term is a historiographic convention and slightly anachronistic. The honorific of ''Augustus'' was not used until the reign of the Pontifex Maximus Gnaeus I, who ruled in the late 1st and early 2nd century AD. However, it is the preferred nomenclature because of the swift succession of constitutional responsibilities of the chief officer of state from Pontifex to Magister Militum and finally to Emperor that occurred over the course of the 2nd and 3rd centuries AD. Though the constitutional positions changed, the role in the state of the man holding the title of Augustus remained similar throughout this period, and so it is applied to all three offices by historians as a shorthand.

articles.title: Auraicum
articles.snippet:
{{stub}}

'''Auraicum''' was a province of [[Great Levantia]] situated along the upper [[Auara River]] basin, with its northern borders based on the [[Calidus River|Calidus]] and [[Maruva River]]s while its southern perimeter sat along the [[Chrisos River]] and the highland elevation of central Dericania. It roughly corresponds to the eastern half of [[Rhotia]] though it crossed into northeastern [[Lapody]] as well. The province was established in the wake of the campaigns of [[Gaius Stephanus Pictor]], who established [[Colpira|Colonia Pictoria]] as a preliminary staging area for Levantine conquests during the [[Caballian Wars]]. Colonia Pictoria was the seat of the provincial administration, though for a time [[Pusego]] overshadowed it in terms of economic relevance. Auraicum was primarily connected to the rest of Great Levantia by the ''[[Via Nauria]]'', which crossed the central Dericanian steppe and connected the [[Norteven River]] to the Auara's tributary of the [[Nauros River]].

'''Celticization''' refers to the process by which the ancient [[Latinic people]]s who founded [[Great Levantia]] and populated its urban areas gradually adopted elements of Celtic culture, including dress, vocabulary, diet, and other customs. The process occurred throughout the majority of southern Levantia and also applied to the people of the [[Decapolis]], part of the [[Ancient Istroyan civilization|ancient Istroyan civilization]]. This process was foundational in establishing the cultures of modern [[Urcea]], [[Rhotia]], [[Lapody]], [[Burgundie]], and other parts of [[Catholic Levantia]]. While scholars agree that Celticization occurred, they disagree sharply on the extent of it and especially the timeline of its occurrence.

articles.title: Optimate_(Urcea)
articles.snippet:
'''Optimates''' (''"best ones"'') were the class of nobility in [[Urcea]] and existed through the early 20th century. For a time, optimates were the primary political actors in Urcea as well as its [[Feudalism in Urcea|primary land-owning class]]. The optimate nobility was greatly weakened by the [[Saint's War]] but continued as an important political force until the [[Crown Regency]] at the end of the 19th century.

==Structure and qualifications==
In order to be enrolled as an Optimate, the head of a family must meet an extensive property requirement for three generations. While the property requirement varied greatly through the era, the methodology for being enrolled remained the same. During an enrollment period, the individuals in question had to retain the minimum property requirement the entire time of the enrollment, although they could go below it once enrolled. articles.title: Privilegiata
articles.snippet:
{{Award winning article}}
The '''Privilegiata''' ("privileged") were a class within the traditional system of [[social class in Urcea]]. Originally, this class mostly included members of the [[Optimate (Urcea)|optimate nobility]] who had lost wealth to the degree that they fell out of the nobility. However, over Urcean history, they gradually expanded to become a quasi-middle class and major political force within the social and economic life of [[Urcea]].
==Initial structure==
Initially, the privilegiata were a class consisting of individuals who had lost their optimate status. Former optimates could never become freemen and thus became this class, which still conferred with it certain social and economic privileges without as many of the obligations. These privileges included a minimum wage, the first of its kind in [[Levantia]]. articles.title: Provincia_Levantina
articles.snippet:

'''Provincia Levantina''' was a province of [[Great Levantia]] in the center of the empire. It was centered around the [[Norteven River]] basin, extending to the [[Scrovan River]] in the east, the [[Ionian Mountains]] in the south, the Nortevan to the west, and the central Deric highlands to the north. The province was so named due to its status as the first organized province, consolidating the conquests of Levantia in northwest [[Dericania]]. The political and economic center of the province was [[Pareto]], though [[Carsula]] and [[Carinella]] were also major cities. Ruxbur
articles.snippet:
[[File:Mace_head_(4872682650).jpg|thumb|A 2<sup>nd</sup> century BC ''xótiruxbur'' from [[Cascada]] State]]
A '''ruxbur''' is an {{wp|eating utensil}} used in [[Coscivian civilisation|Coscivian cultures]]. A ''xótiruxbur'' or "long ruxbur" comprises a spherical or polyhedral base covered in spines and affixed to a shaft. Its general appearance may be compared to a {{wp|Morning star (weapon)|spiked mace}}. A ''sekmeruxbur'' ("short ruxbur") comprises a convex rounded surface with the spikes affixed to the outer side and a lateral handle or series of thongs on the inner side to facilitate manipulation by the diner. While eating, the diner spears pieces of food, usually several, with the ''ruxbur'', before drawing them to the mouth for consumption. 

The ''ruxbur'' developed from the use of {{wp|sea urchin}} {{wp|Test (biology)|tests}} as utensils by coastal Coscivians. "Fresh" ''ruxbur'' fashioned directly from urchins are still commonly used at seafood restaurants and for ritual meals.

'''The Kukki Sisters''' were a [[Metzetta|Metzettan]]-born female singing trio who made their career in [[Urcea]] following the [[Second Great War]], becoming the first Metzettan musical act to chart outside of [[Alshar]]. They appeared over 20 times on Urcean television and released two popular albums there, as well as releasing several records at home. The group consisted of Haneul, Aja and Misun, referred to as Hannah, Ada and Michelle in Urcea, respectively. Haneul and Aja truly were sisters, however Misun was merely their cousin. The group is sometimes credited as kickstarting the popularity of Metz-pop, though the term wouldn't be coined for several decades to come.

articles.title: Vigintiquinque
articles.snippet:
The '''vigintiquinque''' (Latin: "''twenty five''"), also often called simply the '''tribes''', were the primary social and kinship grouping within [[Great Levantia]] among its Latin, citizen population. As understood by modern historians, the tribes were not families in the sense of a single genetic affinity, but rather groupings of families and lineages which were grouped together going back to the earliest days of Latin history in Levantia. The tribes were represented in the [[Tribal Assembly (Great Levantia)|Tribal Assembly]]. The tribes are distinguished in Levantine history primarily by their {{wp|nomen}}, the second part of a {{wp|tria nomina}}. Families within the twenty five tribes were distinguished by a {{wp|cognomen}}, the third name within the tria nomina.
